ut_reids_basin.blurb: Reids Basin is a small, high-elevation crag in the Uinta Mountains of northeast Utah, with fourteen routes, mostly bolted and a couple of trad lines. The wall is horizontally fractured quartzite, and the grades span from the 5.7 range up to 5.12, with most of the climbing between 5.10 and 5.12. The walk in is about a mile, so it is a quick outing by mountain standards, and it tends to stay quiet. Expect cool, changeable weather even in summer: bring warm layers and a rain shell, because afternoon storms roll in. There is still room for new lines.

ut_low_standard_cave.blurb: Low Standard Cave is a small sport crag on the Maple Canyon Road in central Utah, set close to the campground so the walk from the car is only a few minutes. Every route is bolted, around fourteen in total, running from the 5.10s up through 5.13, with the bulk of them in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. It sees fewer visitors than much of the canyon, which makes it a handy spot for a few quick burns, though grades here can feel on the stiff side compared with neighbouring walls.

ut_westwind_buttress.blurb: Westwind Buttress is a trad-only buttress in Little Cottonwood Canyon in Utah's central Wasatch, holding about fourteen routes. Grades start around 5.8 and reach into the 5.12s, with the middle of the range, 5.8 through 5.10, making up most of the lines. Several are multi-pitch, and a few of the harder ones are considered among the better routes on the buttress. Bring a standard trad rack; this is a place for climbers comfortable placing their own gear rather than clipping bolts.

ut_george.blurb: George is a small wall in Rock Canyon above Provo, in the southern Wasatch, with about fourteen routes: a bit more than half bolted and the rest trad. The climbing centres on an overhanging arete and the face beside it, and the lines run from easy 5.4 territory through the 5.7 to 5.10 range that suits intermediate climbers, with a single 5.12 at the top end. Bolted anchors cap the sport lines. It sits a short way up the canyon from the parking at the mouth, and it is less busy than the walls beside the trail.

ut_empire_pass.blurb: Empire Pass is a small bouldering area, a rock garden just east of the pass about four miles south of Park City, at roughly 9,000 feet. It holds fourteen problems, mostly low-to-the-ground and friendly, from very easy up to about V4, with most falling between V0 and V3. Landings on the free-standing boulders are described as safe, which makes it a relaxed spot for beginners and a quick stop for anyone passing through. Expect sun, wind and cool air up here.

ut_petrified_hornet_wall.blurb: Petrified Hornet Wall is a trad-only wall in Indian Creek, southeast Utah, with about fourteen routes. It is a sandy face sitting between two better-known neighbouring walls. Every line is trad, on the sandstone the Creek is known for, and the difficulty sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, roughly half of them at 5.10, so this is a place for climbers who already have some Creek experience rather than newcomers. Unclimbed ground remains on the wall for anyone looking to add something new.

ut_schoolroom_southern_buttress.blurb: Schoolroom Southern Buttress is the southern end of the Schoolroom cliffs above Ogden, with fourteen routes split evenly between sport and trad. Climbs range from easy 5.6 up to 5.10, and half of them are 5.10, so it suits climbers already comfortable on moderate-to-hard terrain. The buttress mixes single-pitch and multi-pitch lines, and a 70 m rope is useful on some of them. Most routes are grouped under the Center Stage sector, with a few more in a smaller sector called Coupler Area.
